evidence_text: Olo's Q4/FY2023 investor press release (2024-02-29) explicitly names Five Guys as having deployed Engage GDP (Guest Data Platform) and Marketing. Olo's named-customer case study (olo.com/case-studies/five-guys-engage) attributes a $2M revenue lift during the first six months and describes an enterprise rollout after an initial 150-location group, eventually covering Five Guys' full footprint. This supports GDP/Marketing usage specifically -- not a claim that Five Guys uses Olo Pay or Olo for core online ordering beyond its existing relationship.
source_title: Olo Q4/FY2023 investor press release + Five Guys Engage case study
limitations: Rollout location count is vendor-stated, not independently verified as a current live count. Supports GDP/Marketing only, not Olo Pay or core ordering.

evidence_text: The live Google Play listing for Del Taco's 'Del Yeah! Rewards' app (package com.olo.deltaco, update shown 2026-05-27) is published under Olo's own package namespace and advertises points for in-store/online purchases, personalized offers, and ahead ordering for pickup, drive-thru, delivery, and Park & Get It. This is evidence of an Olo-associated mobile ordering/loyalty surface specifically -- it does not establish Del Taco's POS, KDS, or payment processor.
source_title: Google Play: Del Taco -- Del Yeah! Rewards
limitations: App-store package namespace is strong implementation evidence but the listing copy does not name the contracted Olo product(s) or prove enterprise-wide deployment.

evidence_text: Presto's FY2024 Q3 Form 10-Q (filed 2024-05-21) disclosed that during the nine months ended March 31, 2024, Del Taco decided not to continue Presto Voice -- superseding Presto's January 2023 press release announcing an expansion of Presto Voice AI at Del Taco drive-thrus. This relationship should be recorded as ENDED/historical, not current; the filing does not state a replacement vendor.
limitations: Filing does not state the reason, exact end date, site count, or any replacement voice-AI vendor. Do not infer a current voice-AI provider for Del Taco.

evidence_text: Olo publicly lists Order, Pay, and Engage suites: Order includes online ordering, Serve front end, Dispatch, Rails, Catering+, loyalty, Order with Google, and Switchboard; Engage includes GDP, marketing, and sentiment. Olo says its platform is open/modular with 400+ integration partners; its Summer 2024 release documents an Ordering API, Dispatch API, store-hours API, and POS synchronization for Rails tips. Customer proof: Five Guys Engage GDP+Marketing case study, $2M six-month revenue lift claim, rollout from a 150-location group. Likely vulnerability: vendor-authored proof, multi-product catalog overlaps with a merchant's existing POS/payments/loyalty/CRM/ordering tools -- validate active modules, contract ownership, data portability, and incremental cost before positioning a Genius replacement. Value wedge: position Genius as the unified cloud POS/payments/ops suite (75+ native integrations, open API per Global Payments' own restaurant materials), then prove it can preserve/connect the customer's chosen digital/guest layer rather than claiming feature parity with Olo's GDP/marketing.
source_title: Olo product pages + Summer 2024 release notes + Five Guys case study
limitations: Comparative Genius-vs-Olo positioning is a discovery hypothesis, not a verified customer-stack assertion.

evidence_text: PAR positions Brink as a configurable cloud POS with an open API/integration ecosystem. Big Chicken case study: selected Brink, PAR Pay, Data Central, and hardware/services, citing open API, integrations, and real-time operations data as buying criteria. Roberto's Taco Shop case study: using Brink since 2023, citing faster service and forced end-of-day closure. Both are vendor-authored case studies -- do not treat as proof of price, uptime, implementation duration, processor freedom, or outcomes for a new prospect. Confirm actual integrations, payment routing, support SLAs, and migration burden in discovery; no direct PAR-Genius integration claim is made anywhere in this evidence.
source_title: PAR Brink case studies (Big Chicken, Roberto's Taco Shop)
limitations: Vendor-authored case studies only; no independent verification of price, uptime, or processor terms.

evidence_text: Presto's 2023-01-10 press release claimed an expansion of Presto Voice AI at Del Taco drive-thrus, with >95% of orders completed without staff intervention at cited test locations, feeding POS/KDS. Presto's own FY2024 Q3 Form 10-Q (2024-05-21) later disclosed Del Taco decided not to continue Presto Voice -- the pilot/expansion did not persist. Treat performance claims as vendor-authored; require current-site reference calls, intervention/accuracy metrics, rollout scope, staffing model, and reason for termination before citing this vendor as a live customer proof point.
source_title: Presto Del Taco expansion release (2023) + FY2024 Q3 10-Q (2024)
limitations: The only named customer example (Del Taco) ended the deployment; treat as a diligence flag, not a customer-proof asset, until a currently-live reference is found.
